title: Numbers 0–20
sourceNote: The auto-captions garble every number word; they were reconstructed from standard German. The sample phone number in the video was unclear, so the examples here are invented and marked as supplementary.
objectives: I can count from 0 to 20 in German
I can pronounce the special sounds in the numbers (s, z, ei, ü, ig)
I can build the numbers 13 to 19
I can ask for and give a mobile phone number

patterns.ex: Meine Handynummer ist null eins sieben acht.

grammar.title: Numbers 13 to 19
grammar.body:
Numbers 13 to 19 follow a simple rule: **number + zehn**. Two numbers change a little:

**sechs + zehn = sechzehn** (the -s of *sechs* disappears) and **sieben + zehn = siebzehn** (the -en of *sieben* disappears).
grammar.ar: الأعداد 13–19: العدد + zehn، مع استثناءين: sechzehn و siebzehn.

grammar.title: Sounds in the numbers
grammar.body:
Several letters sound different from English:

**s** before a vowel sounds like English z (*sieben*), but at the end of a word or after the last vowel it sounds like English s (*eins*, *sechs*).

**z** sounds like ts (*zwei*, *zehn*, *zwölf*). **ei** sounds like the English word 'eye' (*zwei*, *drei*). **ie** sounds like 'ee' (*vier*, *sieben*). **eu** sounds like 'oy' (*neun*).

**-ig** at the end sounds like **-ich** (*zwanzig*).

grammar.title: Zahl and Zahlen
grammar.body: **die Zahl** is the singular (one number) and **die Zahlen** is the plural (numbers). The lesson title **Zahlen 0–20** therefore means 'numbers 0 to 20'.

mistakes.why: It is pronounced -ich but always written -ig.

pronunciation.tip: Round your lips as for 'oo' and say 'ee'. *fünf*, *zwölf*.
Round your lips as for 'o' and say 'e'. *zwölf*. There is no English equivalent.
At the end of a word it sounds like -ich. *zwanzig*. Some regions say -ik.

lines.de: Meine Handynummer ist null eins sieben acht.

tip: Say your own mobile number aloud in German, digit by digit. Remember the two exceptions: sechzehn and siebzehn.

comprehension.q: How do you say 12 in German?
What rule forms the numbers 13 to 19?
comprehension.a: number + zehn (for example drei + zehn = dreizehn).

comprehension.q: Which two numbers lose letters when they are combined with zehn?
How is -ig pronounced at the end of zwanzig?

exercises.title: Words to digits
exercises.instructions: Write the number as a digit.

exercises.title: Match the numbers
exercises.instructions: Match each German number with its digit.

summary: The numbers 0–20: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf, dreizehn ... zwanzig.
Numbers 13–19 are number + zehn; exceptions are sechzehn and siebzehn.
Sounds: z = ts, ei = 'eye', ie = 'ee', eu = 'oy', -ig = -ich, and the umlauts in fünf and zwölf.
Ask for a number with Wie ist deine / Ihre Handynummer? and answer Meine Handynummer ist ...
